**Visual analysis of the test image:**

- Single green leaf, noticeably curled/bent downward
- Multiple circular dark brown spots scattered across the upper leaf surface
- Spots vary in size, some small (~3-5mm), some larger (~10mm)
- Spots appear uniformly dark brown to black-ish, some with slightly differentiated borders
- No visible powdery/orange lesions (rules out Rust)
- No pale yellow trails or mines (rules out Miner)
- Leaf is curling at the edges

**Matching against symptom descriptions:**

- **Phoma**: "Circular dark-colored spots of varying sizes on leaves up to 2 cm diameter... leaves curve and may present cracks when lesions reach edges" — the leaf curling is prominent and the spots are circular and dark, matching well.
- **Brown_Eye_Spot / Berry_Blotch**: Require visible grey/light brown centres with dark rings and yellow margins — the yellow halo pattern is not clearly present here.
- **Rust**: Requires orange/yellow powdery lesions on undersides — not present.
- **Miner**: Requires pale yellow trails/mines — not present.
- **Cerscospora**: No symptom description provided.

The combination of circular dark spots of varying sizes **plus the prominent leaf curling** is the clearest match for Phoma.

No yellow halos, powdery lesions, or mining trails are visible to support the other classes."}
